analysis.title: Nomura McElligott - PAUSE 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: Index skew is softening again (puts losing their bid) on 10/23 after what McElligott hypothesizes was 'Peak Risk-Management Unwind' on 10/22. Tech and Energy, the two 'AI Core Constraints', are both up after leading lower the day before, and AI Enablers vs Hyperscalers L/S is also up.

The UST squeeze is pausing. The CTA model shows Systematic Trend would need a substantial further rally to flip the 3-month window back to Long from Short. The 2-week and 1-month windows have already flipped Long after massive buy-to-cover in recent weeks.

'Bonds as Ur Hedge' is working again. Large futures selling in equities and futures buying in USTs on 10/22 looked like asset allocation. The market is assigning more credible delta to a US growth-scare scenario as the 'Cracks in the AI Trajectory' story spreads.

The AI outlook shifted from 'Heads I Win, Tails You Lose' to 'Glass Totally and Completely Empty'. After negative sentiment catalysts across the AI equity ecosystem over the past week, positioning saw large-scale capitulation, following a rebuild of longs in September's 'Agentic Excitement' and the return of sizeable speculative upside options trades in the usual AI names.

The AI trade is a 'Pick Your Poison'. If hyperscaler capex keeps accelerating as META showed, the market focuses on negative FCF and the ability to finance it, with 'More Paper at Wider Spreads'. If capex decelerates, it undercuts the best-case AI demand, adoption and profitability scenario that was priced in.
Thematic risk-premia stop-outs on 10/22 were violent. Nomura's L/S monitor showed 124 US pairs stopped out, of which 47 moved more than 3 sigma, 26 more than 4 sigma and 6 more than 5 sigma.

McElligott attributes the stop-out and capitulation to crowding in a year of widespread 'High Sharpe Winners' in carry and trend. With Q4 performance pain after rolling unwinds in fixed-income macro RV and equity thematics/momentum, traders are in 'De-risking and Shut-It-Down' mode to survive drawdowns before the new-year PnL reset, rather than buying reversals in the prior winners.

Carry took body blows and momentum reversed hard. CTA shorts in bonds and STIRs are being covered, with $68B of bond futures and $38B of STIRs covered over the past 2 weeks. Signals remain Short, so more covering is possible if the squeeze continues. Legacy longs in equities, USD and commodities saw substantial implied deleveraging.

The AI thesis reset is squeezing still-extreme crowding in legacy UST/STIRs shorts and payers. The CTA signal moved from -100% short to -74% short. Rate vol showed a positive spot-vol correlation on 10/22 (USTs up, vol up), a change from much of the year when vol rose with higher rates.

Equities flipped back to negative spot-vol correlation after much of 2026 with higher realized vol on up days than down days. The shift is most acute in Nasdaq and SMH, where realized vol is again larger on down days.

S&P and VIX moved little relative to the pain in crowded AI/tech positions. 'Reverse Dispersion' (tech longs hit, shorts in rate-sensitives and everything else squeezed higher) kept index correlation low. McElligott argues multi-strat market-neutral funds are now the incremental leveraged equity dollar, which makes 'Corr 1' moves rare without a macro tail shock.

Notable flow ahead of a big week (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT earnings, ORCL investor day, Anthropic S-1 possibly as early as 10/23 night, and the Fed meeting): a paper seller of SPX Dec 7900 / Jan 7300 risk reversal, tied at 7655, selling 4000x at 54.00. McElligott reads it as selling skew and marking a line in the sand.

Call buying resumed in core AI names over the past week: CRWV ($69M premium, 3M shares delta or $170M), NBIS ($25.7M premium, 500k shares delta or $80M) and DRAM ($20M premium, 1.9M shares delta or $85M).

A key to 'Reverse the Reversal' is VRP and premium-income options sellers selling the vol rip, including QIS programs selling 0DTE gamma. Customer flows stuff dealers and pin the market. Futures rallied back to unchanged on 10/23, which McElligott says checks the stabilizing-flow box (buying weakness, fading strength) and should help realized vol re-compress.

sector_views.rationale: AI trade framed as 'Pick Your Poison': accelerating hyperscaler capex raises FCF and financing worries, while deceleration undercuts priced-in best-case AI demand. Crowded longs were stopped out on 10/22.

earnings_insights: Meta's accelerating hyperscaler capex plans are cited as the example behind FCF-burn and financing worries. No EPS or revenue figures given.
Hyperscaler earnings (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT) are due in the week after 10/23, along with an ORCL investor day. No estimates given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Short covering has cut the extreme short signal. The 2-week and 1-month windows are Long, and the 3-month window needs a substantial further rally to flip Long.
Listed with hyperscaler earnings as a major event risk for the week.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex either accelerates (FCF burn, financing cost, wider spreads) or decelerates (undercuts priced-in AI demand).
A US growth scare gaining delta as cracks in the AI trajectory spread.
Q4 drawdown-avoidance de-risking by crowded trend and carry funds.
Further CTA covering in bonds and STIRs if the squeeze resumes.
Event risk in the coming week: GOOGL, AMZN and MSFT earnings, ORCL investor day, Anthropic S-1 and the Fed meeting.
vol_and_positioning: Index skew is softening, with puts losing their bid, on 10/23 after the 10/22 unwind.
Nasdaq and SMH are back to negative spot-vol correlation (larger realized vol on down days), after much of 2026 with higher realized vol on up days.
Rate vol showed a positive spot-vol correlation on 10/22 (USTs up, vol up), unlike much of the year.
S&P and VIX moved little relative to AI/tech pain. Reverse dispersion kept index correlation low.
CTA covering over the past 2 weeks: $68B of bond futures and $38B of STIRs. The CTA signal in bonds went from -100% short to -74% short.
Thematic L/S stop-outs on 10/22: 124 US pairs, 47 beyond 3 sigma, 26 beyond 4 sigma, 6 beyond 5 sigma.
SPX Dec 7900 / Jan 7300 risk reversal sold at 54.00 in size (4000x), tied at 7655.
Upside call buying in CRWV, NBIS and DRAM continued over the past week.
Premium-income and VRP sellers, including QIS selling 0DTE gamma, are the key stabilizer to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: Continued hyperscaler capex acceleration supports the AI demand, adoption and profitability thesis that was priced in.
tension_points.bear_case: Accelerating capex raises FCF burn and financing concerns (more paper at wider spreads). Deceleration would undercut the priced-in best-case AI demand scenario. Either outcome hits the AI trade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT) and capex guidance in the coming week.

tension_points.bull_case: Futures rallied back to unchanged, skew is softening, and premium-income sellers and 0DTE QIS flows pin the market, letting realized vol re-compress.
tension_points.bear_case: Equities are back to negative spot-vol correlation and a growth scare is gaining delta, with crowded AI longs having been stopped out.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Premium sellers not selling the vol rip, and the stabilizing-flow pattern (buying weakness, fading strength) failing.
